mosques.name: Masjid al-Haram
mosques.significance: The holiest site in Islam, home to the Kaaba
mosques.description: Masjid al-Haram, also known as the Grand Mosque, is the largest mosque in the world and surrounds Islam's holiest place, the Kaaba, in the city of Mecca. Muslims around the world face the Kaaba during their five daily prayers.
mosques.history: The mosque surrounds the Kaaba, the ancient house of worship believed built by Prophet Ibrahim. Expanded through the centuries—under Caliph Umar (638), Ottoman Sultan Selim II (1571), and Saudi expansions (1950s onward)—it is the focal point of Hajj and Umrah.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may not enter. Hajj visa required for pilgrimage. Dress modestly; Ihram for Hajj. Best visited during Ramadan or Hajj season for spiritual atmosphere.

mosques.name: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
mosques.significance: Second holiest site in Islam, burial place of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
mosques.description: The Prophet's Mosque is the second-holiest site in Islam, built by Prophet Muhammad himself in 622 CE. It houses the tomb of the Prophet and is one of the largest mosques in the world with its iconic green dome.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Classical Islamic with Ottoman and Modern elements
mosques.history: Built by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in 622 CE after the Hijrah. The green dome marks the Prophet's burial place. Successively expanded by Umayyads, Abbasids, Mamluks, Ottomans, and Saudi rulers.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may not enter. Visitors need valid visa. Women pray in designated areas. The Rawdah (green carpet area) is highly sought—visit early morning for shorter queues.

mosques.name: Al-Aqsa Mosque
mosques.significance: Third holiest site in Islam, destination of the Prophet's night journey
mosques.description: Al-Aqsa Mosque, meaning 'The Farthest Mosque', is located in the Old City of Jerusalem. It is the third-holiest site in Islam and was the original qibla (direction of prayer) before Mecca.
mosques.history: Construction began under Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik (685 CE); completed by his son al-Walid I (705 CE). The Dome of the Rock enshrines the Foundation Stone. Al-Aqsa mosque lies south.
mosques.architectureNotes: Early Islamic architecture with Byzantine and Persian influences. Gold dome, blue and turquoise tilework, marble columns.
mosques.tourismNotes: Check current access and security. Modest dress required. Non-Muslims may visit the compound at designated times.

mosques.name: Imam Reza Shrine
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosque complexes by area, shrine of Imam Reza
mosques.description: The Imam Reza Shrine is a complex containing the mausoleum of Imam Reza, the eighth Imam of Twelver Shia. It is the largest mosque in the world by dimension and the second most visited religious site in the world.
mosques.history: The shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth Imam of Twelver Shia Islam, was established in 818 CE after his martyrdom. The complex grew under Samanids, Safavids, and Qajars.
mosques.architectureNotes: Persian-Islamic style with turquoise domes, golden minarets, and intricate tilework (kashi-kari).
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit most areas. Dress modestly; women need chador (provided). Peak pilgrimage during Nowruz and Ramadan.

mosques.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in the world, architectural masterpiece
mosques.description: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is one of the most beautiful mosques in the world, featuring 82 domes, over 1,000 columns, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet. It's open to visitors of all faiths.
mosques.history: Commissioned by Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, founder of the UAE. Completed in 2007, it honors Islamic and global cultures.
mosques.architectureNotes: 82 domes, 1,000+ columns, 24-carat gold chandeliers, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet. White marble and semi-precious stone inlays.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required; abayas provided for women. Best time: morning. Photography allowed. Closed Friday morning.

mosques.name: Hassan II Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Africa, built on the Atlantic Ocean
mosques.description: Hassan II Mosque stands partially over the Atlantic Ocean, with a retractable roof and the world's tallest minaret at 210 meters. It's a masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship and one of the few mosques open to non-Muslims.
mosques.history: Built to commemorate King Hassan II's 60th birthday. Construction 1986–1993. Designed by French architect Michel Pinseau. Minaret at 210 m is the world's tallest.
mosques.architectureNotes: Traditional Moroccan zellige tilework, carved wood, and plaster. Retractable roof over the main prayer hall.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Tours run several times daily.

mosques.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed)
mosques.significance: Iconic Ottoman mosque, known for its blue tiles
mosques.description: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is famous for its hand-painted blue tiles adorning its interior. With six minarets and a magnificent dome, it's one of Istanbul's most iconic landmarks.
mosques.history: Built 1609–1616 by Sultan Ahmed I. Architect Sedefkar Mehmed Agha drew on Hagia Sophia and Mimar Sinan. Six minarets caused controversy; Sultan funded a seventh at Mecca.
mosques.architectureNotes: Famous for 20,000+ hand-painted blue Iznik tiles. Central dome 43 m high. Six minarets. Classic Ottoman layout.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Closed during prayer times. Modest dress; scarves and robes provided. Opposite Hagia Sophia in Sultanahmet.

mosques.name: Faisal Mosque
mosques.significance: National mosque of Pakistan, unique tent-like design
mosques.description: Faisal Mosque is the national mosque of Pakistan, located at the foot of Margalla Hills. Its unique design resembles a desert Bedouin tent, blending contemporary architecture with traditional Islamic elements.

mosques.name: Istiqlal Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Southeast Asia, symbol of Indonesian independence
mosques.description: Istiqlal Mosque is the national mosque of Indonesia and the largest mosque in Southeast Asia. Its name means 'Independence' in Arabic, commemorating Indonesian independence. It features interfaith dialogue, standing across from Jakarta Cathedral.

mosques.name: Grand Jamia Mosque
mosques.significance: Among the world's largest mosques by capacity, Pakistan's largest
mosques.description: The Grand Jamia Mosque in Bahria Town Karachi is one of the world's largest mosques by capacity. Its design is inspired by the Selimiye Mosque in Turkey, featuring stunning Ottoman architecture with modern amenities.

mosques.name: Badshahi Mosque
mosques.significance: Iconic Mughal-era mosque, one of Pakistan's most visited landmarks
mosques.description: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673. It is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture and was the largest mosque in the world for over 300 years. Its red sandstone and marble make it one of Lahore's most iconic sights.
mosques.history: Built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673. The largest mosque in the world for over 300 years until Faisal Mosque (1986).
mosques.architectureNotes: Red sandstone and marble. Symmetrical courtyard, octagonal minarets, Persian calligraphy.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Modest dress required. Located near Lahore Fort. Best in morning light.

mosques.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
facilities: One of world's largest chandeliers and carpets
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Oman, open to non-Muslim visitors
mosques.description: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque was completed in 2001 and can hold 20,000 worshippers. It features one of the world's largest hand-loomed carpets and a massive Swarovski crystal chandelier. Non-Muslims are welcome outside prayer times.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome outside prayer times. Modest dress required; abayas provided. One of world's largest chandeliers and carpets.

mosques.name: Putra Mosque
mosques.significance: Iconic pink-domed mosque and Putrajaya landmark
mosques.description: The Putra Mosque is known for its distinctive rose-tinted granite and stunning location on Putrajaya Lake. Completed in 1999, it combines Malay and Persian design and is one of Malaysia's most photographed mosques.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitor access. Rose-tinted granite. Waterfront location on Putrajaya Lake. Photography allowed.

mosques.name: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin Mosque
mosques.significance: National symbol of Brunei, one of Asia's most beautiful mosques
mosques.description: Built in 1958, this mosque stands in an artificial lagoon and is crowned by a golden dome. It blends Mughal and Malay styles and is one of the most photographed religious buildings in Southeast Asia.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitor viewing. Stands in artificial lagoon. Golden dome. One of Southeast Asia's most photographed mosques.

mosques.name: Baitul Mukarram
mosques.significance: National mosque of Bangladesh
mosques.description: Baitul Mukarram is the national mosque of Bangladesh, completed in 1968. Its design avoids the traditional dome and instead uses a contemporary interpretation of the Kaaba, making it distinctive among modern mosques.

mosques.name: Taj-ul-Masajid
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in India
mosques.description: Taj-ul-Masajid means 'Crown of Mosques.' Construction began in the 19th century and was completed in 1985. Its pink facade and vast courtyard make it one of the largest and most striking mosques in India.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
mosques.significance: Largest adobe building in the world, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick (adobe) building in the world. Rebuilt in 1907, it is a pinnacle of Sudano-Sahelian architecture and is replastered annually by the community. UNESCO World Heritage since 1988.
mosques.history: Rebuilt in 1907. UNESCO World Heritage since 1988. Largest adobe building in the world. Replastered annually by the community during the Crepissage festival.
mosques.architectureNotes: Sudano-Sahelian style. Mud bricks, wooden beams (toron) protruding from walls. Three minarets.
mosques.tourismNotes: Interior access for non-Muslims is limited. Best viewed from outside during the annual replastering festival.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Kuwait
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Kuwait
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Kuwait was completed in 1986 and can accommodate over 11,000 worshippers. It houses a large Islamic library and is known for its elegant design and one of Kuwait's largest prayer carpets.

mosques.name: Jama Masjid
mosques.significance: India's largest mosque, Mughal architectural masterpiece
mosques.description: Jama Masjid in Old Delhi was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan and completed in 1656. Built of red sandstone and white marble, it features three domes and two 40-meter minarets. The courtyard can hold 25,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Built by Shah Jahan 1644–1656. Same emperor as the Taj Mahal. The mosque faces west toward Mecca.
mosques.architectureNotes: Red sandstone and white marble. Three domes, two minarets. Symmetrical courtyard. Persian and Indian influences.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Modest dress required; robes provided. Climb minaret for city views. Closed during prayer. Near Chandni Chowk.

mosques.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the world's oldest universities, center of Islamic learning
mosques.description: Al-Azhar Mosque was founded in 970 CE by the Fatimid Caliphate. It houses Al-Azhar University, one of the world's oldest degree-granting universities. A center of Sunni Islamic scholarship for over a millennium.
mosques.history: Founded 970 CE by Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz. Al-Azhar University established 988. Expanded by Mamluks and Ottomans. Major center of Islamic scholarship.
mosques.architectureNotes: Fatimid foundation with Mamluk and Ottoman additions. Multiple minarets from different eras. Marble, stucco, wood carvings.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required. Near Khan el-Khalili bazaar. Combine with Islamic Cairo tour.

mosques.name: Islamic Center of Washington
mosques.significance: First major mosque in Washington D.C., diplomatic and cultural landmark
mosques.description: The Islamic Center of Washington was dedicated in 1957. Designed by Italian architect Mario Rossi, it blends traditional Islamic architecture with modern elements. Serves the diplomatic community and visitors from around the world.
mosques.history: Founded by Muslim diplomats. Dedicated 1957. President Eisenhower attended. Designed by Mario Rossi in Mamluk style.
mosques.architectureNotes: Mamluk-inspired. Minaret 50 m. Persian carpets, Turkish tiles, Egyptian woodwork. Stained glass.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome. Modest dress required; abayas provided. Near Embassy Row. Free tours.

mosques.name: Imam Ali Shrine
mosques.significance: One of Shia Islam's holiest sites, tomb of Imam Ali
mosques.description: The Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf is the burial place of Imam Ali, the fourth Caliph and first Imam of Shia Islam. One of the world's largest mosque complexes by capacity and area, it attracts millions of pilgrims annually.
mosques.history: The shrine was established in 977 CE. Rebuilt and expanded many times. The golden dome and minarets were added in Ottoman and Qajar eras. A major center of Shia scholarship.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required; abayas provided for women. Check travel advisories before visiting.

mosques.name: National Mosque of Malaysia
mosques.significance: National mosque of Malaysia, modernist Islamic architecture
mosques.description: The National Mosque of Malaysia was completed in 1965. Its distinctive folded plate roof and 73-meter minaret make it a landmark of Kuala Lumpur. Designed by a team of three architects in a modernist Islamic style.
mosques.history: Built to commemorate Malaysian independence (1957). Completed 1965. Named Masjid Negara.
mosques.architectureNotes: Folded plate concrete roof instead of traditional dome. 73 m minaret. Capacity 15,000.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome outside prayer times. Modest dress required; robes provided. Near Lake Gardens and KL Bird Park.

mosques.name: Djamaa el Djazaïr
mosques.significance: Africa's largest mosque, world's third-largest mosque
mosques.description: Djamaa el Djazaïr, also known as the Great Mosque of Algiers, was completed in 2019. It features the world's tallest minaret at 265 meters and is the largest mosque in Africa.
mosques.history: Construction 2012–2019. Designed by KSP Jürgen Engel Architekten. World's tallest minaret (265 m).
mosques.architectureNotes: Contemporary design with traditional elements. 265 m minaret. Interior space 20,000 m². Seismic-resistant.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Located on the Bay of Algiers.

mosques.name: Birmingham Central Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the UK's largest and oldest purpose-built mosques
mosques.description: Birmingham Central Mosque opened in 1975 and serves one of the UK's largest Muslim communities. Its golden dome and minarets are a prominent landmark in the city.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Contact for tour arrangements.

mosques.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
mosques.significance: Masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, imperial mosque
mosques.description: The Süleymaniye Mosque was built by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent and completed in 1557. Perched on one of Istanbul's seven hills, it dominates the skyline and is considered Sinan's greatest work.
mosques.history: Built 1550–1557 by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Süleyman. The complex includes tombs of Süleyman and his wife Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana). Damaged by fire in 1660, restored.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four minarets (ten balconies total). Central dome 53 m high. Courtyard with ablution fountain. Ottoman classical layout.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Modest dress required. Closed during prayer. Located in Fatih, near Grand Bazaar.

mosques.name: National Mosque
mosques.significance: National mosque of Nigeria, landmark of Abuja
mosques.description: The National Mosque in Abuja was completed in 1984 and serves as the national mosque of Nigeria. Its golden domes and minarets are a prominent landmark in the capital city.
mosques.history: Completed 1984. Designed by AIM Consultants. National mosque of Nigeria, located near the National Christian Centre.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Contact for tour arrangements.

mosques.name: Abdul Rahman Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Afghanistan, central Kabul landmark
mosques.description: The Abdul Rahman Mosque, also known as the Grand Mosque of Kabul, is one of Afghanistan's largest mosques. Built on 1.4 hectares in the heart of Kabul, it features 19 domes, two minarets, and a three-story prayer hall with a dedicated women's floor.
mosques.history: Construction began in 2001 by businessman Hajji Abdul Rahman. Major work completed in 2009; officially inaugurated July 2012 by President Karzai.
mosques.architectureNotes: 19 domes, 2 minarets, 44 arched windows around the main dome. Prayer hall 56×24 m with three floors.

mosques.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Amman, only mosque in the city open to non-Muslim visitors
mosques.description: The King Abdullah I Mosque was built as a memorial to Jordan's founding king. Its distinctive blue mosaic dome dominates the Abdali skyline. The only mosque in Amman that openly welcomes non-Muslim visitors.
mosques.history: Built 1982–1989 by King Hussein as a memorial to his grandfather King Abdullah I. Octagonal prayer hall with no interior pillars.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blue mosaic dome 35 m diameter, 31 m high. Main hall holds 3,000; courtyard 3,000; women's section 500.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome. Modest dress required; abayas and headscarves provided free. Islamic Museum inside.

mosques.name: Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab Mosque
mosques.arabicName: جامع الإمام محمد بن عبد الوهاب
facilities: Separate ablution halls for men and women
mosques.significance: Qatar's largest mosque, national grand mosque
mosques.description: The Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab Mosque, also known as Qatar State Grand Mosque, is Qatar's largest mosque. It features 93 domes—28 large domes over the central hall—and accommodates over 30,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Refurbishment and expansion began December 2006; inaugurated 2011. Named after the 18th-century Islamic scholar.
mosques.architectureNotes: 28 large domes, 65 smaller domes. Sandstone facades. Central hall air-conditioned for 10,000+ men; 1,300 women in separate areas.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to all visitors during non-prayer times. Modest dress required; scarves and abayas provided. Photography prohibited in ladies' area.

mosques.name: Al-Fateh Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Bahrain, national mosque
mosques.description: The Al-Fateh Grand Mosque is Bahrain's largest mosque, named after Ahmed Al-Fateh, the founder of Bahrain. It features one of the world's largest fiberglass domes and Italian marble throughout.
mosques.history: Opened in 1988. Serves as place of worship and educational center. One of the largest fiberglass domes in the world.
mosques.architectureNotes: Italian marble flooring, teakwood doors from India, ornate chandeliers. Large fiberglass dome.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required; abayas provided. Near Bahrain National Museum.

mosques.name: Massalikoul Djinane Mosque
mosques.significance: West Africa's largest mosque, commemorates Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba
mosques.description: Massalikoul Djinane is West Africa's largest mosque, inaugurated in 2019. Built to commemorate Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba, founder of the Mouride Brotherhood, it features five minarets, Carrara marble, and a chandelier with 2,000 lights.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Contemporary Islamic with West African influences
mosques.history: Construction took over 15 years. Inaugurated September 27, 2019. Built to commemorate Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba. 75 m height; minaret pinnacle 80 m.
mosques.architectureNotes: Five minarets, Carrara marble, golden columns. 10,000 in prayer hall; 20,000 on esplanade.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. West Africa's grandest mosque.

mosques.name: Heydar Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Azerbaijan and the Caucasus region
mosques.description: Heydar Mosque is the largest mosque in Azerbaijan and the Caucasus. Completed in 2014, it features four 95-meter minarets and a 55-meter main dome. The complex can accommodate 75,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Construction began September 2012; opened December 26, 2014. Designed by Ədalət Məmmədov. Named after former President Heydar Aliyev.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four minarets 95 m high. Main dome 55 m; second dome 35 m. Interior area 4,200 m².

mosques.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
mosques.significance: Downtown Beirut's iconic Blue Mosque, largest Sunni mosque in Lebanon
mosques.description: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, known as the Blue Mosque for its light blue tiles, dominates downtown Beirut near Martyrs Square. Commissioned by former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, it was inaugurated in 2008.
mosques.history: Construction began 2002 following donation by PM Rafic Hariri. Inaugurated 2008. Hariri buried adjacent in Martyrs Square. Damaged in 2020 Beirut explosion but structure intact.
mosques.architectureNotes: Five blue-tiled domes, 48 m main dome, four minarets 65 m. Designed by Azmi Fakhoury.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Near Martyrs Square and Mohammad Al-Amin Square.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Khartoum
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Sudan, historic Turkish-Islamic style
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Khartoum, also known as Al Kabir Mosque, is Sudan's largest mosque. Built in Turkish-Islamic style with reddish sandstone, it was opened in 1901 and accommodates up to 10,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Built 1900; officially opened 1901 when Khedive Abbas II of Egypt visited during Anglo-Egyptian Sudan. Center of old Khartoum.

mosques.name: Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest historical mosque in Bosnia, representative Ottoman structure in the Balkans
mosques.description: The Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque, built in 1530, is the largest historical mosque in Bosnia and Herzegovina. A masterpiece of Early Ottoman architecture, it was the first mosque in the world to receive electric illumination in 1898.
mosques.history: Built 1530 as part of Gazi Husrev-beg's endowment (madrasa, marketplace, hammam). First mosque with electricity 1898. Restored after Bosnian War.
mosques.architectureNotes: Central dome 13 m diameter, 26 m high. Minaret ~36 m. Five marble columns, portico with five cupolas. Cut stone construction.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome outside prayer. Modest dress required. In Baščaršija, heart of old Sarajevo.

mosques.name: Hazrat Sultan Mosque
mosques.annualVisitors: Second largest mosque in Central Asia
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Kazakhstan, second largest in Central Asia
mosques.description: Hazrat Sultan Mosque opened in 2012 and is Kazakhstan's largest mosque. Its 51-meter dome and four 77-meter minarets dominate the Astana skyline. The complex covers over 11 hectares.
mosques.history: Opened July 6, 2012. Built in classical Islamic style. Second largest in Central Asia after Turkmenbashi Ruhy.
mosques.architectureNotes: Dome 51 m high, 28.1 m base diameter. Four minarets 77 m. Construction area 17,700 m².
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Near Bayterek Tower and Khan Shatyr.

mosques.name: Al-Zaytuna Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in Tunis, hosted one of Islam's first universities
mosques.description: Al-Zaytuna Mosque, the Mosque of the Olive, is the oldest mosque in Tunis and hosted the University of Ez-Zitouna—one of the first and greatest universities in Islamic history. Its 160 columns were brought from the ruins of Carthage.
mosques.history: Founded c. 698–732 CE. Modeled on Great Mosque of Kairouan. University of Ez-Zitouna established. Scholars included Ibn Khaldun, Ibn 'Arafa.
mosques.architectureNotes: Prayer room 56×24 m (1,344 m²). Minaret 43 m. Trapezoidal courtyard, columns with marble capitals.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required. In medina of Tunis, near souks.
